title: Finite coefficient extension preserves the uniform Tor interval
statement: Fix finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ramification index $e$ defined by $\varpi_E\mathcal O_F=\varpi_F^e\mathcal O_F$, and let $W$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ with all reductions of Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$, define $C_{F/E,W}(K)=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$. Then every $F$-level reduction of $C_{F/E,W}(K)$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$. More explicitly, at level $m$ choose $n$ with $en\ge m$; the reduction is $K_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{F,m}$, and tensoring with any degree-zero $A_{F,m}$-module $N$ identifies the test with $K_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}N$, so no flatness of $A_{F,m}/A_{E,n}$ is required. Use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] for the coefficient levels, completeness and derived tensor.

source.place: Unit Step 2: ordinary derived coefficient extension preserves the finite-Tor domain

proof.text: Write $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$, $A=A_{E,n}$ and $C=A_{F,m}$, where $m\geq1$ is arbitrary and $n$ is chosen with $en\geq m$. Since $\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_F=\varpi_F^{en}\mathcal O_F\subseteq\varpi_F^m\mathcal O_F$, the reduction $\mathcal O_F\to C$ kills $\varpi_E^n$, so $\mathcal O_E\to C$ factors through $A$; on limit projections the two ring maps $R\to S\to C_W$ and $R\to A_W\to C_W$ agree. Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ over $R$ with flat terms. Then $P\otimes_RS$ is K-flat over $S$ with flat terms and $Q=P\otimes_RA_W$ is K-flat over $A_W$ with flat terms, and $Q$ represents $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$; $P\otimes_RS$ represents $C_{F/E,W}(K)$. Hence the $F$-level reduction $C_{F/E,W}(K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_F}A_{F,m}$ is represented by $(P\otimes_RS)\otimes_SC_W$, which by associativity of termwise change of rings along $R\to S\to C_W$ and $R\to A_W\to C_W$ equals $P\otimes_RC_W=Q\otimes_AC_W$, a representative of $K_n\otimes^L_AC$. The derived change-of-rings statement makes these identifications independent of $P$. No flatness of $C$ over $A$ is used.

source.place: first paragraph: exactness and cofinal reductions

proof.text: Let $N$ be any sheaf of $C_W$-modules placed in degree zero. Since $Q\otimes_AC_W$ is K-flat over $C_W$, the derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor] computes $(K_n\otimes^L_AC)\otimes^L_CN$ as the total tensor complex $(Q\otimes_AC_W)\otimes_CN$, which is termwise and as a complex equal to $Q\otimes_A\operatorname{Res}N$, where $\operatorname{Res}N$ is $N$ regarded as a sheaf of $A_W$-modules by restriction of scalars. As $Q$ is a K-flat resolution of $K_n$, this complex computes $K_n\otimes^L_A\operatorname{Res}N$. By hypothesis $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, so by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] applied to the degree-zero $A_W$-module $\operatorname{Res}N$ its cohomology sheaves vanish outside $[a,b]$. Thus every $F$-level reduction of $C_{F/E,W}(K)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, the same interval for all $m$. The test only uses restriction of scalars along $A\to C$, never flatness of $C$ over $A$.

source.place: first paragraph after displayed reductions: constructibility and uniform Tor bounds

proof.text: The quotient identifications are compatible with transition maps in m, so the complexes just described form the normalized F-tower of the completed scalar extension. The normalized-DVR effectivity statement identifies its derived-limit object with these reductions and gives derived completeness. The completed scalar comparison identifies $C_{F/E,W}(K)$ (K is derived complete) with the strict-tower integral scalar extension, and the integral scalar-extension constructibility theorem places the resulting object in the bounded constructible category; together with the uniform [a,b] calculation above, it lies in D^b_ctf(W,\mathcal O_F) and has the asserted interval at every F-level.
